name: base-s3
description: ESP32-S3 base controller: 5-24 V DC, PoE plug-in and USB-C power with INA226 per input, W5500 Ethernet, four 5 A low-side MOSFET outputs on a separate load input, 2x8 expansion bus.
notes: DRAFT, NOT REVIEWED. 120x90 mm, 4 layers, GND pours on inner1 and bottom. Open doubts to resolve before fabrication: (1) Load path: 4 x 5 A = 20 A through the load terminals (two KF2EDGR 2P in parallel, 15 A per pin), a 2 mOhm shunt and the GND return; the autorouter does not size traces for this, so VLOAD, OUTn and the load GND return need hand-drawn wide copper or pours, and probably 2 oz copper. No fuse or reverse-polarity protection on the load input (reverse connection conducts through the MOSFET body diodes and flyback diodes). (2) AON6354 is driven straight from 3.3 V GPIO; its datasheet rates Rds(on) at 4.5 V and 10 V, not 3.3 V, so check the Rds(on) curve at Vgs = 3.3 V before trusting 5 A. Thermal vias under the drain tab were removed from the EasyEDA footprint because they had no net and would have shorted to the GND pours; add drain-net copper instead. (3) Surge vs INA226: SMBJ26A on the DC and load inputs clamps around 42 V at full surge current, above the INA226 40 V absolute maximum; fine for 12 V and regulated 24 V supplies, marginal for 24 V lead-acid systems (28.8 V charging is near the TVS breakdown). An 85 V monitor (INA238 class) would remove this but was not found in JLCPCB stock. (4) TPS54360 buck: output set to 4.88 V (51k/10k) at about 610 kHz (RT 160k); compensation (16.9k, 4.7nF, 47pF) is a starting point, not a worked loop; EN floats (internal pull-up), no UVLO divider; check with TI WEBENCH. The PowerPAD footprint is hand-written (3.1 x 2.4 mm pad, no thermal vias yet). (5) Logic power OR-ing uses SS56 Schottky diodes (about 0.5 V drop): DC and PoE onto VIN, USB VBUS onto 5 V. With USB only, 5 V sits near 4.5 V and can back-feed the buck output; with DC present the buck wins at 4.88 V. INA226 sit before the diodes so each reads its own source. (6) PoE: the HR911105A has no line-side centre taps, so the PoE plug-in (J_POE, 12 V in) has no way to take power from the cable through this jack. Needs a PoE-capable magjack or discrete magnetics, or an external splitter into the DC input. (7) W5500 front end (49.9R terminations, 6.8nF RX centre, TX centre tap to 3.3 V) and the HR911105A LED pin polarity (pins 9-12) are from memory and the EasyEDA symbol; check against the WIZnet reference schematic and the HanRun datasheet. (8) Antenna: the module antenna sits at the top edge but the GND pours run under it; cut the pours back under the antenna. (9) USB: 5.1k CC resistors give a 5 V-only sink; no series resistors on D+/D-. (10) Diodes and LEDs use pinLabels cathode=pin1 to match the LCSC footprints; check orientation in the CPL before ordering. (11) DRC: the pours and power footprints have not been through a KiCad rule check, and the JLCPCB export has not been through the JLCPCB uploader.
